standard.title: Electric Traction Lifts — Part 3: Safety Rules — Section 1: Passenger and Goods Lifts (विद्युत कर्षी लिफ्ट — भाग 3: सुरक्षा नियम — अनुभाग 1: यात्री और माल लिफ्ट)
standard.sector: Electrotechnical / Lifts, Escalators and Moving Walks

standard.description: This Indian Standard prescribes the essential safety rules, mechanical and structural parameters, electrical protection, clearances, and testing procedures for the design and construction of electric traction passenger and goods lifts to safeguard users, maintenance mechanics, and emergency rescue teams.

certification.description: Mandatory Certification under various State Lift Acts & Rules (e.g., Delhi Lift Rules, Maharashtra Lift Act). Licences to operate elevators are granted by State Lift Inspectors only upon verifying compliance with the safety rules of IS 14665, with key certified components carrying the physical ISI mark.
requirements: Observed or calculated final test values, maximum net car areas, clearances, and emergency battery back-up capacities must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

Strict limits are set on the inside car area relative to rated loads to prevent hazardous overcrowding. Car dimensions are measured panel-to-panel at a height of 1 m from the finished floor (e.g. 4 passengers / 272 kg requires a net area of 0.68 to 0.77 sq m).

Under Amendment No. 1, every passenger lift must carry an automatic overload sensor. If loaded to 110% of capacity or more, the car must remain stationary with doors fully open, and activate an audio-visual alarm.

Under Amendment No. 1, all passenger lifts must have a battery-operated ARD to automatically move the car to the nearest landing during power cuts. It must open doors and activate an audio-visual trapped passenger indicator. Capacity must sustain at least 3 rescue cycles.

No lift can start or run unless all landing doors are closed and mechanically locked. Positive electromechanical interlocks must physically confirm lock engagement before the safety circuit is completed.
The lift car must be equipped with natural ventilation openings or fans and emergency battery back-up lighting to operate during power failures to prevent occupant panic.
